answer: Use `show ssh-host-key-<public-key-algorithm>` (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). These are the global SSHv2 host keys, used by both server-side and client-side SSHv2 based apps. There must be one host key per supported algorithm, so yes, more than one exists. The system auto-generates a host-key in the default DB, and additional host-keys can be added or overwritten via the ssh-keygen RPC. The public-key-algorithm values are ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096 and ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 support starts in R9.0). Each entry shows public-key (OpenSSH/PEM string, 0..2048 chars), label (0..256 chars), fingerprint-algorithm (md5 or sha256) and fingerprint (0..95 chars, pairs of hex digits). `show ssh-host-key` lists all; `show ssh-host-key-ecdsa-sha2-nistp521` shows one.

`ssh-keygen [-b=<key-length>] [-l=<key-label>] [-t=<type>]` (Operational mode) generates a private/public key pair, and the existing keys in the system are replaced with the newly generated pair. `-t` selects rsa, ecdsa or ed25519, default rsa. `-b` sets strength: RSA 2048/3072/4096, ECDSA 256/384/521, ED25519 256. With secure-mode enabled (see security-policies/secure-mode) RSA only supports 4096 and ECDSA supports 384 or 521 (default 384); with secure mode disabled RSA supports 2048, 3072 or 4096 (default 2048) and ECDSA supports 256, 384 or 521 (default 256). ED25519 is 256 regardless of secure mode. `-l` sets the key label; if omitted the label is the value of ne-id. Retrieve the new public key with `show ssh-host-key`.

Create an SSHv2 known-hosts entry: `add ssh-known-host-<id> address <value> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value> [label <value>]`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `id` is a unique name, String 0..64 characters. `address` is the hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address of the allowed/known peer host, and may carry a zone index after a % sign for link-local addresses. `public-key-algorithm` is one of ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, ecdsa-sha2-nistp384, ecdsa-sha2-nistp521, ssh-rsa2048, ssh-rsa3072, ssh-rsa4096, ssh-ed25519 (ED25519 support starts in R9.0). `public-key` is the OpenSSH host public key in PEM form, String 0..2048 characters. `label` is a user defined String 0..256. Afterwards only `set ssh-known-host-<id> label <value>` is settable; use `show` to view and `delete ssh-known-host-<id>` to remove.

The `trusted-certificate` object holds the X509v3 CA (Root and Intermediate) certificates trusted by the system. Use `show trusted-certificate[-id]` to view version (v3), serial-number, subject-name, issuer, trust-chain (leafref to /ne/system/security/certificates/trusted-certificate/id), valid-from, valid-to, modification-time, status (in-use, unused, revoked, expired, available, pending-import, invalid, untrusted, future, valid, unsupported), public-key-length (rsa2048/rsa3072/rsa4096/ecdsa256/ecdsa384/ecdsa521), public-key-type (rsa, ecdsa), signature-key-type (rsa, ecdsa, rsassa-pss), signature-hash-algorithm (sha256, sha384, sha512, sha1), certificate-bytes, key-usage and extended-key-usage. Settable: revocation-mode (auto, force-revoked, force-unrevoked; default auto), alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default allowed) and label. Removal is done with `clear certificate`. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Issue `terminate cable-id` (Operational mode) to stop all running CableID verification tests. Because verification is performed on a port-pair basis, the test can only be terminated after the current port-pair verification completes and before the test starts for the next port-pair: the in-progress port-pair runs to completion, then the test exits. The maximum delay to terminate is one port-pair verification time. The test is known to be terminated once cable-id-status `cable-id-state` changes to *idle*, so after issuing the command use `show cable-id cable-id-status` to confirm the cable-id entity is back in the idle state. Related: `show cable-id` lists the cable-id entities; the test itself is started with the `verify` command.

The CableID signal can only be sourced or terminated by CAD10A and RD20TM sleds; the signal is transparently passed in the OPSM. The CableID path starts at the *end A* port and terminates at the *end Z* port, where the signal is sourced/terminated, that is at a CAD10A DWDM port or an RD20TM ADE port. Accordingly `show cable-id-path-<name>` reports card-type-a and card-type-z with values RD20TM or CAD10A, plus port-a and port-z (port AIDs). The card type is derived from the provisioned fiber-connection at the port-A/port-Z attribute: when a fiber-connection is created, the CableID function examines whether it is associated with a port on a CableID capable sled and, if so, captures that card type into the CableID path topology. In R8.0.1 the supported sleds are CAD10A and RD20TM.

Yes. `show cable-id-status [cable-id-state] [test-progress]` is the container holding the process status and progress information of a CableID-based fiber connection verification, and you are allowed to issue `show cable-id cable-id-status` at any time to query the progress. `cable-id-state` is idle (verification not running), running-incl-switching (running for both active and protected paths) or running-no-switching (running only for the active path); default idle. `test-progress` is a string (0..255 chars), default 'None': it reads "Not applicable" if cable-id-state is disabled, or "N out of M completed" while running, where M is the total number of port-pairs to be tested and N the number of port-pairs whose testing has completed. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Each carrier can discover up to one node. It is possible for multiple collocated carriers to discover the same node multiple times, each time connected to a different remote carrier. Use `show carrier-neighbor-<local-carrier> [last-update] [age] [local-carrier-id] [ne-id] [ne-name] [ne-type] [remote-carrier-id] [ipv4-loopback-address] [ipv6-loopback-address]` in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `local-carrier` is the local carrier instance that discovered the neighbor node (string 0..16). ne-id and ne-name are strings 0..256, ne-type 0..64, remote-carrier-id 0..64 and is the AID of the remote carrier connected to the local carrier, implying a specific remote port id. last-update is a date-time in YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ format. The loopback addresses may be empty if not configured.

Use `show connection-ports-<degree-number>/<index> [port-name]` in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `degree-number` is a uint16 in range 1..20 and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. `index` is a uint32 in range 1..2 but is always 1 in the 1830 GX, since dwdm-line ports are bi-directional. `port-name` is an instance-identifier pointing to the dwdm-line port of an RD or ILAx card; as a consequence the OMS of the corresponding dwdm-port is created. `show connection-ports*` lists every connection port in the node, for example connection-ports-1/1 -> port-1-3-dwdm-line1, connection-ports-5/1 -> port-4-1-dwdm-line1. `show connection-ports-5/1` shows just that one entry.

Use `show custom-tlv-<lldp-port>/<direction>/<oui>/<subtype> [value]`, which shows the list of Organizational Specific TLVs (Type-Length-Value) parameter information. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `lldp-port` is the local port associated with the LLDP agent, string length 0..64. `direction` is the direction associated with the LLDP statistics, ingress or egress. `oui` is the Organization Unique Identifier of this TLV, the hexadecimal representation of the 24 bit identifier, string length 1..6. `subtype` is the sub-type identifier of the TLV within the scope of that OUI, string length 1..507. `value` is the retrieved TLV content.

No. The external-fiber-connection is set autonomously by TNMS, and although it is possible to configure it manually, it is not recommended to do so. It is the physical link representation of a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations. Syntax: `add external-fiber-connection-<name> src-port-name <value> dst-port-name <value> [label] [scope] [src-node-id] [src-card-name] [dst-node-id] [dst-card-name] [fiber-connection-type]`. Before R8.0 the user also had to set port external-connectivity to *yes*. `scope` is general-purpose (default) or cable-id; if scope is not cable-id the CableID verification excludes the connection. After upgrade to R8.0.1 or later scope defaults to general-purpose, so to enable CableID you must delete the existing entries and add new ones with scope cable-id. fiber-connection-type is one-way or two-way, default two-way.

A `fiber-connection` is the physical link representation of a connection between two distinct ports (or two distinct sub-ports) in the same NE, in an OADM/ILA topology. An `external-fiber-connection` is the physical link representation of a connection between two ports of L0 cards in different NEs, or in the same NE in disaggregated configurations, and it is set autonomously by TNMS (manual configuration is possible but not recommended). fiber-connection takes `name` (0..64 chars), `label` (0..256), `src-port` and `dst-port` as instance identifiers, and `fiber-connection-type` one-way or two-way, default two-way; add/set/show/delete are all available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode with no pre- or post-condition. external-fiber-connection instead uses string src-port-name/dst-port-name plus node-id and card-name fields, and adds the `scope` attribute (general-purpose or cable-id).

Yes. `icdp` is the Nokia Carrier Discovery Protocol, and its only attribute `global-switch` is a flag to enable icdp with values true or false and a default of true, so the protocol is on by default. Use `set icdp global-switch <true|false>` to change it and `show icdp [global-switch]` to view it, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The icdp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Example: `set icdp global-switch true`.

INCI is the Inter-NE Communication Interface, an API based communication infrastructure for control plane communication across different network elements, for example between a Transponder (such as CHM6 on 1830 GX G40) and line systems (FLEXILS). It uses gRPC server/client as the core mechanism: when the INCI service is enabled the gRPC server starts and binds to the local IP address, and when an INCI neighbor instance is configured gRPC client sessions are established. It is not running by default: the `inci-enabled` switch takes true or false with a default of false. Enable it with `set inci inci-enabled true` and check with `show inci [inci-enabled]`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode.

Compare the `configured-node-name` you provisioned against the `discovered-node-name` reported by the far end. `configured-node-name` is the user provisioned name of the remote NE, string 0..128, and is explicitly used to compare against the discovered-node-name; `discovered-node-name` is the name of the remote NE as sent by the remote NE, string 0..128. `discovered-node-id` (string 0..12) gives the node ID of the remote node as received from it. Use `show inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> [neighbor-address] [neighbor-port] [connection-status] [configured-node-name] [discovered-node-name] [discovered-node-id] [alarm-report-control] [oper-state]`. Both names are supplied at creation: `add inci-neighbor-<neighbor-id> neighbor-address <value> configured-node-name <value> [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>]`, where alarm-report-control defaults to inhibited and oper-state is enabled or disabled.

Two attributes on `interface-neighbor` control this. `discovery-cycle-time` is the periodicity at which sndp discover messages are sent, range 30..300 seconds, default 30. `discovery-timeout` is the time after which discovery is considered failed; when this timeout occurs the neighbor-adjacency-state transitions to blackout. Its range is 300..1800 seconds, default 300. Set them with `set interface-neighbor-<local-interface> [discovery-cycle-time <value>] [discovery-timeout <value>] [discovery-enabled <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>]` in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `discovery-enabled` is true or false, default true. `neighbor-adjacency-state` shows blackout, discovery, holding or unknown, default unknown; oper-state is enabled or disabled, default disabled.

No. `show links` displays the links container within the topology, and these links are dynamically filled in by the system, allowing the NCT topology to be derived and displayed. The command takes no parameters and is available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The related `show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port>` shows NCT connectivity information, the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE, and those links are likewise dynamically filled in by the system.

The global `lldp` object carries a single attribute, `hold-on-timer`: the time to keep neighbor information in case the neighbor does not have an explicit Time-To-Live (TTL) TLV. It is a number of seconds and defaults to 900. Use `show lldp [hold-on-timer]` to view it and `set lldp [hold-on-timer <value>]` to change it, for example `set lldp hold-on-timer 60`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The lldp object is managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted. Per-neighbor, `show lldp-neighbor` reports a `ttl` giving the number of seconds until the remote system information expires; if the remote system does not provide a ttl value, that parameter is set to the global hold-on-timer.

`show lldp-local-info-<lldp-port> [chassis-id-subtype] [chassis-id] [port-id-subtype] [port-id] [port-description] [system-name] [system-description] [supported-capabilities] [enabled-capabilities]` shows the LLDP local system information sent on an lldp-port. chassis-id-subtype is chassis-component and the 1830 GX NE uses the chassis serial number as chassis-id. port-id-subtype is local and the NE uses the port AID as port-id. port-description uses the port name, system-name uses the NE name, and system-description uses the string 'Nokia Corporation.Converged OS, Version <release id> _ build <software label>'. All these strings are 0..255 characters. supported-capabilities and enabled-capabilities take router and bridge. `show lldp-local-info` covers all LLDP ports; example for an AUX port: `show lldp-local-info-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4`.

No, the egress direction is not supported. `show lldp-neighbor-<lldp-port>/<direction>` shows the LLDP remote system discovered by the lldp-port, and the `direction` key, the direction in which the neighbor was detected, only takes the value ingress. Example: `show -r lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-1-3/ingress`, or `show -r lldp-neighbor-comm-eth-1-11-ETH4/ingress` for an AUX port on a 1830 GX G30. The same restriction applies to `lldp-port-statistics`, whose direction parameter is also ingress only. Neighbor information is kept indefinitely, until the port is decommissioned or the data is manually cleared by the user. Attributes include last-update, age (seconds since discovery), chassis-id-subtype/chassis-id, port-id-subtype/port-id, port-description, system-name, system-description, supported/enabled-capabilities and ttl.

No. All counter values in a particular `lldp-port-statistics` entry are maintained on a continuing basis and are not deleted upon expiration of the TTL timing counters associated with the LLDP neighbor information. All statistical counters associated with a particular port on the local LLDP agent do become frozen whenever `lldp-admin-status` is disabled for that port. Use `show lldp-port-statistics-<lldp-port>/<direction> [last-change-time] [last-clear-time] [total-ageouts] [total-discarded-frames] [error-frames] [total-frames-in] [total-frames-out] [total-discarded-tlvs] [total-unrecognized-tlvs]`; direction is ingress (egress is not supported). total-ageout counts the times a neighbour's information was deleted from the lldp-neighbor list due to TTL timer expiration. All counters default to 0; last-clear-time defaults to 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z.

Use `show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port> [src-chassis] [dst-chassis] [src-chassis-state] [dst-chassis-state]`, which gives NCT connectivity information, the existing links between NCT ports in a multi-chassis NE, dynamically filled in by the system. `src-chassis-state` and `dst-chassis-state` take node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned, so the controller shelf shows as node-controller and shelves not yet accepted show as unprovisioned. src-port and dst-port must be NCT ports: if the port belongs to a commissioned chassis it is the AID of the port, and if it belongs to an unprovisioned chassis it has the format '<chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>'. Likewise src-chassis and dst-chassis are the chassis AID when commissioned and the chassis serial number when unprovisioned. All are strings 0..64. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The `sndp` command controls the SNDP feature through a single attribute, `sndp-enabled`, which is a switch with values true or false and a default of true. Use `set sndp [sndp-enabled <value>]` to change it and `show sndp [sndp-enabled]` to view it, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. SNDP is the discovery mechanism behind interface neighbors: `interface-neighbor` `discovery-cycle-time` is described as the periodicity at which sndp discover messages will be sent (30..300 seconds, default 30), and per-interface discovery is separately controlled by `discovery-enabled` (true/false, default true).

`add submarine-link-<name> src-node-id <value> src-port-name <value> dst-node-id <value> dst-port-name <value> degree-target-tx-power <value> [...]`. The mandatory attributes are src-node-id and dst-node-id (the NE names of the source and destination nodes, strings 0..256), src-port-name and dst-port-name (the OTS dwdm-line port of the degree at each endpoint, strings 0..128), and degree-target-tx-power, the target transmit power for the degree, the launch power at the ROADM into the primary fiber link. `fiber-length` defines the fiber length in km of the associated fiber pair ID, a decimal64 in range 0..25000 km with default 0, and it excludes the length of the branch segments. Other attributes: label, src/dst-card-name, fiber-connection-type (two-way default, two-way only for submarine links), link-name, fiber-pair-id, segment-list, bu-segment-index (uint16, default 0), rx/tx-fiber-type, gsnr, degree-expected-rx-power, commissioning-snr-margin, launch-condition (flat-tx or pfib, default pfib) and allocated-spectrum-list (start/end frequency pairs, max 32 elements).

`show supporting-fiber-connection-<name> [fiber-connection-list]` shows the list of fiber connections supporting an entity. `name` is the name of the entity, String 0..64, and `fiber-connection-list` is the supported fiber connection path, an instance-identifier. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. It is the container referenced by cable-id-path: `show -r cable-id-path-<name>` displays the supporting-fiber-connection container and its fiber-connection-list along with all cable-id-path parameters for the port pair, for example output lines 'supporting-fiber-connection-1-6-ade6-1-8-ade6' and 'fiber-connection-list  supporting-fiber-connection-R1'.
